surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Rangers roll past the Canucks
paras: Tye Kartye opened the scoring for the Rangers just 27 seconds into the game, but Jake DeBrusk made it 1-1 for Vancouver late in the first. Will Cuylle put the Rangers up 2-1 early in the second. Elias Pettersson (#25) tied it up for Vancouver shorthanded late in the period, but they didn’t score again. Kartye struck again a minute and a half later to put the Rangers ahead 3-2. Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault scored just under five minutes apart early in the third to make it 5-2, and the Canucks never had an answer. Cuylle scored again with less than five minutes left to make it 6-2.

The Rangers drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Dylan Garand made 19 saves for the Rangers, and Kevin Lankinen allowed six goals on 25 shots. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Vladislav Gavrikov, by our Swing measure. The Rangers improved to 5-2-0, and the Canucks fell to 2-5-0.

items.text: The Canucks are on a four-game losing streak.
Alexis Lafrenière has a point in four straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.
Tye Kartye scored his first two goals of the season, his first since Apr 15.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
